CheckTitle: Snowflake accounts configure a minimum Time Travel retention period
Description: **Time Travel** retention determines how far back a table's prior state can be queried or restored. This check verifies that the account sets a retention period of at least one day, and reports where the minimum is left at zero.
Risk: With retention at zero, a destructive statement — a mistaken `TRUNCATE`, or deliberate tampering by an attacker covering their tracks — is **immediately unrecoverable**, and there is no prior version to compare against when determining what was changed. Time Travel is often the only mechanism that can establish what a table contained before an incident.

Code.CLI:
ALTER ACCOUNT SET DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS = 7;
ALTER ACCOUNT SET MIN_DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS = 1;
Code.Other:
1. Sign in to Snowsight as ACCOUNTADMIN
2. Set `DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS` to your recovery objective (1 on Standard, up to 90 on Enterprise)
3. Set `MIN_DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS` so an object owner cannot lower retention below the floor
4. Increase retention specifically on databases holding regulated or business-critical data
5. Account for the storage cost of retained versions when choosing the window

Recommendation.Text: Set a Time Travel retention window that matches your recovery objective and enforce a floor with MIN_DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS so object owners cannot reduce it below policy.
